### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. multiple synostoses syndrome 4  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.675)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:4221)

**Proposed mechanism:** GDF6 (HGNC:4221) —DISRUPTS→ BMP signaling pathway (GO:0030521); BMP signaling pathway (GO:0030521) —LEADS_TO→ Vertebral segmentation defects (HP:0004577); BMP signaling pathway (GO:0030521) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal abnormalities (HP:0000977). Loss-of-function mutations in GDF6 disrupt the BMP signaling pathway, leading to vertebral segmentation defects characteristic of Klippel-Feil syndrome and broader skeletal abnormalities seen in multiple synostoses syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in GDF6 associated with gain-of-function mechanisms in either disease would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of GDF6 in these skeletal dysplasias could lead to targeted therapeutic strategies aimed at modulating BMP signaling for the treatment of related congenital anomalies.

#### 2. microphthalmia, isolated, with coloboma 6  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.667)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:4221)

**Proposed mechanism:** GDF6 (HGNC:4221) —DISRUPTS→ BMP signaling pathway (GO:0007178); BMP signaling pathway (GO:0007178) —LEADS_TO→ Vertebral abnormalities (HP:0004408); BMP signaling pathway (GO:0007178) —LEADS_TO→ Microphthalmia (HP:0000590); BMP signaling pathway (GO:0007178) —LEADS_TO→ Coloboma of iris (HP:0000491). Disruption of GDF6 leads to altered BMP signaling, impacting vertebral development in Klippel-Feil syndrome and ocular development in microphthalmia with coloboma.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of pathogenic variants in GDF6 in individuals diagnosed with either Klippel-Feil syndrome 1 or microphthalmia, isolated, with coloboma 6, or identification of pathogenic variants in genes other than GDF6 that consistently cause these phenotypes. _(variant: rs143113930)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of GDF6 in these distinct developmental disorders could inform therapeutic strategies targeting BMP signaling for a broader range of congenital abnormalities.

#### 3. isolated microphthalmia 4  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.666)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:4221)

**Proposed mechanism:** GDF6 (HGNC:4221) —DISRUPTS→ BMP signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-168974); BMP signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-168974) —LEADS_TO→ Vertebral segmentation defects (HP:0004500); BMP signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-168974) —LEADS_TO→ Microphthalmia (HP:0000520). Loss-of-function mutations in GDF6 disrupt the BMP signaling pathway, leading to vertebral segmentation defects characteristic of Klippel-Feil syndrome and microphthalmia observed in isolated microphthalmia 4.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of GDF6 in skeletal and ocular development could lead to novel therapeutic strategies for both Klippel-Feil syndrome and microphthalmia, potentially targeting downstream effectors of BMP signaling.
